question.problem:
Let $C$ be a simple, piecewise-smooth, closed, and positively oriented curve. Given that the line integral

$$
{∮}_{C}P\,\text{d}x+Q\,\text{d}y
$$

 
represents the area of the region $D$ enclosed by any such curve in ${R}^{2},$ which of the following could be the functions $P(x,y)$ and $Q(x,y)?$

I. $P(x,y)={e}^{y}$ and $Q(x,y)={e}^{x}$

II. $P(x,y)=\operatorname{arctan}⁡y$ and $Q(x,y)=y$

III. $P(x,y)=-y$ and $Q(x,y)=y$

current_example.problem:
Let $C$ be a simple, piecewise-smooth, closed, and positively oriented curve. Given that the line integral

$$
\displaystyle \oint\limits_C \mathbf{F} \cdot \text{d}\mathbf{r}
$$

 
represents the area of the region $D$ enclosed by any such curve in $\mathbb{R}^2,$ which of the following could be the vector field $\mathbf{F}(x,y)?$

I. $\left\langle -y, \: y\right\rangle$

II. $\left\langle -2x, \: 2x\right\rangle$

III. $\left\langle 5y\sin x, \: x-5\cos x \right\rangle$
current_example.worked_solution:
According to Green's theorem, if $\mathbf{F}(x,y) = \left\langle P(x,y), \: Q(x,y) \right\rangle,$ where

$$
\dfrac{\partial Q}{\partial x} - \dfrac{\partial P}{\partial y} = 1,
$$

we can write the area of the region $D$ enclosed by the curve $C$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Area}(D) & ={∬}_{D}\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∮}_{C}P\,\text{d}x+Q\,\text{d}y \\  & ={∮}_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r\end{aligned}
$$

  

With that in mind, let's examine each pair in turn.

- Vector field I gives the required area. In this case, 
$\dfrac{\partial P}{\partial y} = -1$
and
$\dfrac{\partial Q}{\partial x} = 0,$
which gives

$$
\dfrac{\partial Q}{\partial x} - \dfrac{\partial P}{\partial y} = 1.
$$

- Vector field II does not give the required area. In this case, 
$\dfrac{\partial P}{\partial y} = 0$
and
$\dfrac{\partial Q}{\partial x} = 2,$
which gives

$$
\dfrac{\partial Q}{\partial x} - \dfrac{\partial P}{\partial y} = 2.
$$

- Vector field III gives the required area. Notice that
$\dfrac{\partial P}{\partial y} = 5\sin x$
and
$\dfrac{\partial Q}{\partial x} = 1+5\sin x,$
which gives

$$
\dfrac{\partial Q}{\partial x} - \dfrac{\partial P}{\partial y} = 1.
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only."
